cory.name: Cory
cory.title: The Optimizer
cory.blurb: Holds the line in person and shreds armour nearby.
cory._abilities:
Unchanged, down to the last number. Cory's Haymaker is what every other slot 1 is modelled on and it is the one the game was tuned against. It has real art in both places now: `icon` is the painted fist that replaced the marked placeholder, and `fx` is the impact burst drawn at him when it lands. 
THE HERO POWER, RESERVED AND NOT YET IMPLEMENTED. The slot is in the bar, the button is wired and it is greyed out and unusable until the hero has transformed -- but `effect` is null and pressing it while powered does nothing except say so. The name is a placeholder chosen to fit the hero; rename it freely when the power is written.

courtland.name: Courtland
courtland.title: The Spark
courtland.blurb: Fast, reckless and always where the trouble is.
courtland._abilities:
COURTLAND'S THIRD REVISION, AND THE ROSTER'S FIRST THREE-ABILITY HERO. He is the test of a more hero-centred shape: one ability in base form, three once he has transformed. Nothing about it is special-cased -- `abilities` is an ordered list of any length and `poweredOnly` is per ability, so the same shape is available to the other four the day somebody wants it.
EVERY NUMBER HERE IS DELIBERATELY OVERPOWERED AND DELIBERATELY UNTUNED, at the request of the child who designed the character. Seismic does 140 in a 150px ring every four seconds, which is more than Cory's Haymaker for less than half the wait; Mind Control turns two enemies for twelve seconds and they hit for 60 while it lasts; the Mind Laser is 42 every 0.15s -- 280 a second -- through armour, for ten seconds of held time. Compare them against the other four heroes before taking any of it as a baseline.
SEISMIC IS SLOT 1 AND IS AVAILABLE IN BOTH FORMS. It replaces Shockwave, which was the same burst under a different name, and it takes `ability-courtland-1` with it -- the ground-shatter icon, which is what that picture always was.
MIND CONTROL fixes a naming mismatch rather than creating one. `ability-courtland-2` is a picture of Courtland gripping an enemy's mind and it was bound to a slot whose data said Seismic; `fx-mind-control` shipped as a marker for a state -- `Enemy.controlled` -- that nothing set. Both are wired to the power they were drawn for. `damage` is what a controlled enemy hits its own side for, on its own attack interval; `radius` is how far from the tapped point the two are looked for; and anything `blockable: false` -- every boss -- is immune, because a boss walks through the line and a boss walking the wrong way through it would be the same bug twice.
MIND LASER is the only `held` ability in the game. `holdSeconds` is the budget of TIME HELD rather than a duration: releasing early keeps what is left, and the cooldown starts when the budget runs out or the finger comes off. `range` is how long the beam is drawn and how far along it enemies are damaged -- fixed rather than ending at the finger, so the beam is still visible with a thumb over the board. `beamWidth` is the corridor's full thickness, so what is drawn is what is hit.

eli.name: Eli
eli.title: The Wall
eli.blurb: Immovable. Holds four at once and never complains.
eli._abilities:
STAR RAIN, AND IT FALLS ON THE WHOLE MAP. Fourteen ninja stars on an 8 second cooldown, ignoring armour, and `coversMap` is the field that says where they land. IT IS STILL A SCATTER, NOT A BLAST: each star only hurts what is within 26px of where it lands (presentation.json heroFx.strikeLength), and which enemy gets how many stars is the roll. What changed is the REACH. It used to be a 62px disc centred on Eli, so the volley was worth about 50 to a lone enemy standing next to him and nothing at all to anything else on the board; Eli asked for it over the entire map and Cory approved it knowing it is overpowered. 
A BIGGER RADIUS CANNOT DO THAT, and this is the arithmetic that decided the shape. A strike damages a 26px disc, which is 2,124 px of a 921,600 px board -- 0.23%. Fourteen strikes scattered uniformly over the playfield would catch a given enemy 0.03 times, and matching the old per-enemy damage that way needs about a thousand strikes. So the volley spreads over the ENEMIES rather than over the empty board: each star picks a live enemy at random, anywhere on the map, and falls within `radius` of it. `radius` is therefore the JITTER round the chosen target now rather than the area, and it is 22 -- inside the 26 a strike damages, so a star that picks an enemy always hits it, and a star that lands on one of a clump still catches its neighbours. The volley is worth hits x damage = 280 either way; it is now delivered wherever the enemies are instead of only where Eli is standing, which is the whole of the buff. With nothing on the board the stars fall over the playfield, so a volley cast on a clear lane looks like the ability rather than like a dead button. 
ICE BEAM. Powered form only, 12.5 seconds like every other slot 2, cooldown reset by the transformation, tap the button then tap inside 260px of him -- the same activation and the same cancel paths as the other four, which is the point of them all sharing one. THE BEAM IS SCENERY. What the power is is a 96px area at the point tapped: everything in it takes 110 and is slowed to 0.18 of its speed for 2.5 seconds. The line drawn from Eli to that point is drawn and nothing else -- an enemy standing between him and the target is not touched, and a test says so, because a beam that hurt what it crossed would be Zoomies with a different colour. THE SLOW IS THE POINT AND IT IS MEANT TO BE SHOCKING: 0.18 against Bramble's 0.45 is a target moving at a fifth of its speed rather than at half, and 2.5 seconds against a tower slow that refreshes forever is a window rather than a condition. A boss that resists crowd control takes the 110 and is not slowed at all -- Enemy.applySlow already refuses on `slowable`, so that costs no code and cannot drift from the towers' version of the same rule. 
RUSSINGA IS FIRE. Eli's third, and the second `held` ability in the game -- Courtland's Mind Laser is the first and this is the same shape in a different element, which is exactly what was asked for. Powered form only. Tap the medallion to arm, then press and hold the BOARD to fire; the beam is `range` long whichever way it points, `beamWidth` is the corridor that is damaged, and `holdSeconds` is a budget of held time rather than a duration, so letting go early keeps what is left. WHILE THE AIM IS NOT ON THE BOARD THE FIRE IS PURELY VISUAL: it spends none of the budget, deals no damage and does not set `fired`, so a press that never reaches the map hands the ability back ready. See GameScene.updateHeldBeam. THE NUMBERS ARE UNDER THE MIND LASER on purpose -- 34 a tick against 42, 8 seconds of hold against 10, and a shorter 420px reach -- because the laser is the roster's declared overpowered outlier and a second copy of it at the same numbers would be two.

bailey.name: Bailey
bailey.title: Good Dog
bailey.blurb: Very fast, very keen, and completely without a plan.
bailey._abilities:
NO DAMAGE AT ALL, deliberately: Bailey is the fastest hero and the weakest, and a slow is worth more to her than a small hit would be. 45% off everything within 112px for 2.5 seconds, on the shortest cooldown on the roster.

_artFacing: WHICH WAY THE ART IS DRAWN, per hero. ALL FIVE ARE 'right', AND THE FIELD IS STILL HERE. Cory used to be the exception -- every frame of him, walk, attack and the SUV, faced LEFT -- and the renderer once carried `both hero sprites are drawn facing LEFT` as a blanket rule with the flip inverted to match, which was true of the only hero there was when it was written and made the four added after him walk backwards. His new art faces right like everyone else's, so there is no per-hero correction left to apply and `mirroredFor` now resolves every hero the same way. The field stays because it is a property of the ART rather than of the roster: the enemies still disagree with each other (five of the twenty are drawn facing left) and they read the same function, so deleting it here would leave one rule with two shapes. `colour` sits beside it for the same reason -- it is a fact about the character.
_note:
THE FIVE HEROES. Cory is first and is the default: a save with no choice in it preselects him, so a player who never touches the row plays exactly the game that was tuned. `poweredSprite` is the form a hero wears once its health has been at or below half.
`ultimateSprite` IS GONE. There used to be two transformations -- the powered form at half health and Last Stand at a quarter -- and the second one had its own sprite field. For all five heroes both fields already named the same picture, and there is one transformation now, so the duplicate is deleted rather than kept in step by hand. `powered` is what that transformation changes about a hero; when it fires, what it takes off incoming damage and how long the grace lasts are `rules.json heroTransform`, because those are facts about the rule rather than about any hero.
`poweredHeight` IS CORY'S ALONE and is the reason it lives here rather than in art.json's `displayHeight`. The Rivian is 1.51:1 -- at the roster's 120px it would be 181px wide, wider than the road it drives over and half again the widest hero. 95 makes it 144 across, which still reads as a vehicle among people. It is a decision about this hero, so it sits with this hero; a hero without the field takes the height its art entry asks for, which is what the other four do.
_stats: DAMAGE PER SECOND IS DELIBERATELY FLAT across the roster: 19 to 24 against Cory's 21.2, a spread of about 12%. Level 1 is tuned to 45 of 60 with Cory, and a hero twice as strong would throw that away the first time anyone picked him. What differs is everything else -- Eli holds four enemies where Bailey holds two, Han reaches 122 where Bailey reaches 70, Bailey moves at 142 where Eli moves at 90 -- so the choice is about how you want to play rather than about which hero is better.
_slots:
ABILITIES ARE A LIST, NOT A PAIR. Every hero declares an ordered `abilities` array and the bar, the cooldown register and the HUD's press handler walk it, so a hero with one ability or with four is data. It was `slot1` and `slot2`, two named fields with two different shapes, and the powered-form gate was the SLOT INDEX -- slot 2 was powered-only because it was slot 2. That could not survive Courtland, who has three abilities of which two are gated, so the gate is `poweredOnly` on the ability itself and how the ability is asked for is `activation`.
EVERY ABILITY DECLARES EVERY FIELD, with zeros where it does not use one -- Bark's `damage: 0` is a statement rather than an omission, and a new ability cannot half-declare itself and read `undefined` as 0 somewhere downstream.
`activation: 'instant'` fires on the press: `punch` hits the nearest enemy hard and throws it back; `burst` damages and briefly stuns everything around the hero; `burn` hits one target and sets it alight; `double` lands two fast hits on the nearest enemy; `howl` damages nothing and slows everything nearby; `rain` scatters `hits` small strikes over `radius`.
`activation: 'targeted'` arms the board and waits for a tap inside `castRadius` of the hero, through the same targeting mode the Ima Dummy rally point uses and with the same four ways out of it -- the CANCEL control, the button again, ESC, and a tap outside the disc. `hazard` leaves a strip on the lane and is the only one that persists; `burst` is a ring of damage at the point; `bomb` is one heavy hit in a small radius; `rain` is a scatter; `dash` sends the hero along the line; `beam` freezes an area at the far end; `control` turns `targets` enemies near the point around for `durationSeconds`, after which they die.
`activation: 'held'` fires while the button is down and is aimed by dragging. `laser` is the only one: a beam `range` long and `beamWidth` thick that charges everything under it every `tickSeconds`, for at most `holdSeconds` of held time.
THE COOLDOWN OF EVERY `poweredOnly` ABILITY RESETS ON TRANSFORMATION, so a hero who has just changed can cast immediately -- a button that becomes usable and is not usable yet reads as the gate being broken.
`colour` is the hero's tint for the placeholder effect art -- see systems/HeroFx.ts -- and every visual is sized to the ability's real radius so the numbers can be judged before the art exists. BALANCE IS A FIRST PASS everywhere except Courtland, whose three are knowingly overpowered; see his own `_abilities`.
